title: UN Begins Sweeping Drawdown in Somalia — Staff Terminations, Asset Sales as US Funding Cutoff Looms
detail: The United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) began visibly executing its drawdown in the week of August 25, 2026: at least 10 civilian personnel on the joint African Union-United Nations Information Support Team were notified their contracts will terminate on September 10, and UNSOS moved forward with plans to auction vehicles, generators, medical supplies, computers, and containers used to support AUSSOM and UN operations. The cuts follow the United States' early-July notice that it will not fund UNSOS — AUSSOM's logistics backbone for fuel, medevac, and engineering support — beyond the mission's December 31, 2026 mandate expiry. Separately, the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) remains on track to complete its transition into a standard UN country team by October 31, 2026. The Somali government pointed to the August 16 graduation of roughly 3,000 newly trained SNA soldiers at Xananbuure, Galmudug, as evidence of its readiness to assume greater security responsibility, though analysts cautioned that expanding troop numbers is not the same as building a self-sustaining national security system.
